response.text:
Locked Workstation Recovery
Overview

This procedure outlines the steps to recover access to a Mint Studios lab Windows desktop when the local Administrator password is unknown and the technician has physical access to the machine. The goal is to regain access to the Administrator account without data loss.

Required Tools and Preparation
A bootable USB drive with a Windows installation media (matching the version installed on the target machine).
A computer with administrative privileges to create the bootable USB (if not already prepared).
Recovery Procedure
Step 1: Prepare the Bootable USB
Ensure you have a Windows installation ISO matching the version on the locked workstation.
Use a tool like Rufus to create a bootable USB drive from the ISO.
Step 2: Boot from the USB Drive
Insert the bootable USB drive into the locked workstation.
Restart the workstation and enter the BIOS/UEFI settings (usually by pressing F2, F12, DEL, or ESC).
Set the USB drive as the first boot device. Save changes and exit BIOS/UEFI settings.
The workstation should now boot from the USB drive into the Windows Setup environment.
Step 3: Access Command Prompt
Once in the Windows Setup, proceed through the initial screens until you reach the "Install now" screen.
Click on "Repair your computer" at the bottom left.
Navigate to "Troubleshoot" > "Advanced options" > "Command Prompt".
Step 4: Reset Administrator Password
In the Command Prompt, type the following commands to replace the Utility Manager with a Command Prompt (this allows you to open a Command Prompt as SYSTEM from the login screen):
copy c:\windows\system32\utilman.exe c:\
copy /y c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe c:\windows\system32\utilman.exe

Restart the computer and remove the USB drive to boot back into Windows.
At the login screen, click on the "Ease of Access" button (or press Windows+U) to open a Command Prompt as SYSTEM.
Type the following command to reset the Administrator password (replace <new_password> with your desired password):
net user Administrator <new_password>

Close the Command Prompt.
Step 5: Restore Utility Manager and Verify
Log in as the Administrator with the new password.
Open Command Prompt as Administrator and restore the original Utility Manager:
copy /y c:\utilman.exe c:\windows\system32\utilman.exe

Verify that the Administrator account is accessible and that all necessary data and applications are intact.
Step 6: Document the Recovery
Document the new Administrator password according to Mint Studios' password management policies.
Record the recovery process in the machine's maintenance log.
Post-Recovery Actions
Ensure the workstation is updated and patched.
Review the machine's configuration and security settings to prevent future lockouts.

By following this procedure, you should be able to regain access to a locked Windows desktop in the Mint Studios lab without losing data.
